faq.q: How do I know if my panel needs an upgrade?
faq.a: Frequent breaker trips, flickering lights, a warm or buzzing panel, and adding large loads are common reasons to have it checked.

faq.q: Do panel upgrades need a permit?
faq.a: In most places, yes, and they are inspected. A licensed electrician normally handles both.

faq.q: Can I upgrade my panel myself?
faq.a: No. Work inside the panel is dangerous and is normally restricted to licensed electricians.

faq.q: Do I need a special circuit for a home charger?
faq.a: Most dedicated chargers do. The size depends on the charger and your vehicle. An electrician sizes it to your panel.

faq.q: Can I plug into a regular outlet?
faq.a: Slow charging from a standard outlet is possible, but a continuous load on a regular outlet needs to be assessed for safety.

faq.q: Does my panel need an upgrade?
faq.a: Sometimes. A load calculation shows whether it has capacity.

services.blurb: Tripping breakers, lost circuits, and flickering lights traced to their cause and repaired.
services.directAnswer: {business} diagnoses and repairs electrical problems across {areas}. A breaker that trips repeatedly is a warning, not a nuisance. Causes include overloads, short circuits, and failing devices. We find the cause and repair it safely. Call {phone}.
process: Ask what happened and when
Test circuits to find the fault
Explain the cause and the repair
Repair, test, and confirm safe operation

faq.q: Why does my breaker keep tripping?
faq.a: Overloaded circuits, short circuits, ground faults, or a failing breaker. A repeated trip means something needs to be found and fixed.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep resetting a breaker?
faq.a: If it trips repeatedly, do not keep resetting it. Have an electrician find the cause.
Loose connections, failing fixtures, or a load on the circuit. A widespread flicker can indicate a bigger issue.

faq.q: What should I do if I smell burning near an outlet?
faq.a: Stop using it. If it is safe, switch off the breaker for that circuit. If you see smoke or flames, leave and call 911.

faq.q: What if a power line is down?
faq.a: Stay far away, keep others away, and call your utility and 911. Do not touch anything in contact with the line.
Any fire, heavy smoke, or someone who was shocked and is injured.
